item.title: Incarico post-doc: Incarico Post-Doc - PSIC-03/B - BEST PRACTICE - Well-being and Stress in the Non-Profit Sector: Research, Analysis, Territorial Engagement, and Intervention Program to Combat Emotional Exhaustion (Univ. TRIESTE)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-09 23:59
Institution: Univ. TRIESTE, Trieste
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PSIC-03 Psicologia sociale, del lavoro e delle organizzazioni

The project aims to map and mitigate psychosocial risks, burnout, and voluntary turnover within Social Promotion Associations (APS) in Friuli Venezia Giulia. Grounded in the Job Demands-Resources Model framework, the study adopts a sequential three-phase mixed-methods design. The first phase, qualitative in nature (a pilot study using focus groups and interviews) conducted at the host APS, will identify sector-specific emotional demands and resources, enabling the development of a psychometric instrument to be used in the second phase. item.description:

Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PAED-02 Ricerca educativa: didattica, pedagogia speciale e pedagogia sperimentale

item.title: Incarico post-doc: The Unconscious in Theories of Language: Between Phenomenology and Psychoanalysis (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-27 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Rome
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PHIL-04 Estetica e filosofia dei linguaggi

Taking as its starting point the fundamental historical and theoretical problems within 20th-century philosophy of language, this project aims to investigate the relationships between French phenomenology and the theory of language—as well as between linguistics and philosophy—incorporating insights from Freudian psychoanalysis. The researcher will focus primarily on the concept of the unconscious, with particular attention to the relationship between language, perceptual processes, praxis, and the institutions of meaning.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Social-psychological processes underlying conspicuous behavior in digital contexts (social networks). (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-04 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PSIC-03 Psicologia sociale, del lavoro e delle organizzazioni

Research aimed at investigating the psychological and social processes underlying conspicuous behavior in digital contexts (social networks). The project examines the role of social motivations, social comparison tendencies, and exposure to—and use of—social networks in the online public expression of status-signaling behaviors. Through the integration of various research designs (cross-sectional, longitudinal, and experimental), possibly involving the collection and quantitative analysis of digital data, the research aims to identify the conditions that foster such forms of expression.
